summary: Polk County 100-foot steel lookout tower reported complete May 1, 1964, beside Cypress Gardens on SR 540-A; the Eastern Lookouts record lists it as removed, with no date.

facts.status_note: The Eastern Lookouts record lists the tower as removed. It gives no removal date and no new site.

events.note: Reported complete in a May 1, 1964 report; described as a 100-foot steel lookout tower
Already manned when completed, per the same report

evidence.supports: 100-foot steel lookout tower, one of eight in Polk County, complete
evidence.quote: The 100-foot Cypress Gardens Fire Tower, one of eight lookout towers strategically located throughout Polk County, is now complete.

evidence.supports: Part of the Florida Forest Service's forest fire detection system
evidence.quote: It's part of the Florida Forest Service's forest fire detection system.

evidence.supports: Located on SR540-A just east of Cypress Gardens, in a station complex with a sub-office, shop and two houses
evidence.quote: The steel lookout tower, located on SR540-A just east of Cypress Gardens, is part of the sub-office, shop and two house complex in this area.

evidence.supports: Towerman, assistant county ranger and families to live on site
evidence.quote: Living on the site when construction is complete, will be a towerman, assistant county ranger and their families.

evidence.supports: Roving ranger and his assistant to work from the station
evidence.quote: Also working from this station will be a roving ranger and his assistant.

evidence.supports: Pick-up tanker and four-wheel drive tanker for wildfire suppression
evidence.quote: A pick-up tanker and a four-wheel drive tanker will make up the woodfire suppression equipment located at the station.
Although just completed, it is already manned

evidence.supports: Eastern Lookouts lists the tower as removed
Park was a botanical garden and theme park near Winter Haven, operated 1936 to 2009
evidence.quote: Cypress Gardens was a botanical garden and theme park near Winter Haven, Florida that operated from 1936 to 2009.

evidence.supports: Owner announced on September 23, 2009 that the park was closing immediately
evidence.quote: On September 23, 2009, owner Land South Holdings LLC announced that the park was closing immediately

evidence.supports: As of 2011, the botanical garden portion preserved inside LEGOLAND Florida
evidence.quote: As of 2011, the botanical garden portion had been preserved inside Legoland Florida

corrections.why: The 1964 report quoted on the page says the tower was part of the Florida Forest Service's forest fire detection system. T29S-R26E is a township and range survey location, not an agency.

notes_for_editor: Tower facts rest on one page, the Eastern U.S. Lookouts entry that quotes a May 1, 1964 Lakeland Ledger report. I did not reach the newspaper. No source found gives the removal date or a new site. Park history comes from Wikipedia only. No source ties the tower's spot on SR 540-A to LEGOLAND Florida, so the story does not say so. Two WebSearch queries turned up no Polk County tower inventory. A RadioReference page lists a modern Cypress Gardens fire station (Sta. #18, 2101 Register Rd, Winter Haven). No source ties it to the 1964 tower, so it is not used. The brief's 30.5 m height matches the 100-foot figure.
